Lessons.Title: Multiply Numbers Larger than 20
ExplanationParagraphs: Source warm-up Number Talk:3×10=30,3×20=60,3×50=150,3×25=75. Knowing3×20=60 makes3×25=60+3×5=75; half3×50=75 also works.

Original Activity1 Clare's 4×23 model contains eight tens and twelve ones=92; Andre's source gridded rectangle has4 rows×23 columns=92. The base-ten model makes four groups of two tens and three ones; regroup80+12=92.

Original Diego diagrams A through D all partition a4×23 rectangle: A widths12+11, B15+8, C10+13, D20+3. Their subareas are48+44,60+32,40+52,80+12; every total92. D is typically easiest because tens and ones are clear; that does NOT mean other partitions are incorrect. Source asks students to choose and justify.
Source3×28=84 (3×20+3×8), using any accurate diagram/symbol model.
Activity2 Some Fine Products: Mai starts2×37 with2×30=60 and completes2×7=14, total74. Original other problems:3×32=96,2×43=86,4×22=88,3×29=87. Teachers assess decomposition and unit-free arithmetic.

Original OPTIONAL Activity3 Play Close to100: number cards0–10, players draw four and use two digits to form a product closest to100, play five rounds, optionally a second more-than20 game. Card draws differ between students; a predetermined answer would be fabricated. Teacher observes strategy.

Original lesson synthesis may ask for3×24, solved72 through place value. Original 7 source image assets viewed on owner device. No publisher image markup or protected Cool-down copied; no runtime tests/Stage D performed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Tens and ones
KeyConcepts.Definition: Decompose larger factors to tens and ones.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent rectangle partitions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Different additive splits preserve total side length and rectangle area.

KeyConcepts.Title: Optional strategic game
KeyConcepts.Definition: Card-draw outcomes vary, so strategy and reasoning are the focus.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Minimize distance |100−product| among current card options.
